newsitem.title: UK: BG extends gain after recent Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: BG extends gain after recent Q1 results.

text.p: Shares in BG Plc rose to a near-post demerger high in active trade on Tuesday, continuing to benefit from recent first-quarter results and lifted by hopes for a regulator's report next month, dealers and analysts said.
The stock was up 7p or 3.5 percent at 204 by 0944 GMT in volume of 6.4 million shares, making it the most active stock in London at that point and the biggest gainer in the FTSE 100 index.

BG, which owns the pipeline network and the natural gas exploration reserves of the former British Gas, was demerged from the natural gas supply business Centrica and made its separate market debut on February 17. Centrica shares were down 3/4p at 61-1/2.
Arthur Hepher, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, highlighted the 40 million stg profit from BG's exploration and production activities in last week's first-quarter results.
"It's been obvious for some time that this is a cheap stock," Hepher said, "and that its valuation depends crucially on the valuation attached to the exploration and production side."
"Last week for the first time people saw profits coming through (from exploration and production) and that has alerted people to the value of the operation."

Hepher added that there could also be hopes for a positive outcome from a report due next month from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, covering price controls on BG's Transco network operation proposed by industry regulator Ofgas.
A report in the Sunday Times last month said BG was set for a victory over Ofgas, with the MMC poised to rule in its favour on a key issue relating to the depreciation of its assets.
The depreciation formula used will have a significant effect on BG's cash flow and its ability to maintain its dividend.
